newsitem.title: UK: Robert Fleming year pretax profits up 25 pct.
newsitem.headline: Robert Fleming year pretax profits up 25 pct.

text.p: British independent investment bank Robert Fleming on Thursday reported pre-tax profits of 167.6 million pounds ($279 million) for the year to March 31, a rise of 25 percent on the previous year's 133.5 million pounds.

The group increased its dividend by 14 percent to 25 pence and Fleming's chief executive William Garrett said in a statement the new financial year had begun well, although the outlook would depend on market conditions.
Robert Fleming year pretax profits up 25 pct =2

Fleming said there had been a very significant increase in profits from its asset management operations in the U.S., Britain and continental Europe. Investment banking had "a busy and profitable year" and securities reported a significant increase in profits.
The group's chairman John Manser said a period of maximum investment strain was over and the results showed Fleming was reaping the rewards of investments made over the last few years.

But Fleming's share of profits from its troubled Jardine Fleming joint venture fell to 37.7 million pounds due to the comparatively poor performance of equity markets in Asia combined with the costs of last year's regulatory investigations into the venture's investment management division.
Fleming said operating income had increased because of strong contributions from all its businesses, while staff numbers remained virtually static at 3,512, compared with 3,428 the previous year.
